title: Maximal-domain identities for a rational extension of an action
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All schemes are separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], where separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Integral means reduced and irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme]; normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Dimensions are topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a smooth integral $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with identity $e$. Products are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $X$ be integral and let $Y\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] with a regular action $a:G\times_kY\to Y$, meaning a morphism satisfying the unit and associativity identities. A rational map means an equivalence class of morphisms on dense open subschemes, taken on its largest open domain of definition. The morphism $a$ followed by $Y\hookrightarrow X$ determines a unique rational map $\alpha:G\times_kX\dashrightarrow X$. Write $g\cdot x=\alpha(g,x)$ whenever defined. For $g,h\in G(k)$ and $x\in X(k)$: if $e\cdot x$ is defined, it equals $x$; if $h\cdot x$ and $g\cdot(h\cdot x)$ are defined, then $(gh)\cdot x$ is defined and equals $g\cdot(h\cdot x)$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, referred rational-action argument; Milne (2013), Definition 4.2 and Lemma 4.3 (graph-closure proof). Local article WANTED; read https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2. No single Stacks tag states the maximal-domain composition assertion.

proof.text: Put $T=G\times_kX$ and $T_0=G\times_kY$. Cover $G$ and $X$ by affine opens. Their coordinate algebras are reduced and finitely generated over the algebraically closed field $k$; [lem-wf-affine-product-reduced] says that each product chart is reduced. Hence $T$ is reduced, since this is checked on an affine open cover. The projection $p:T\to X$ is open by [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open]. Every nonempty open $W\subseteq T$ has nonempty open image $p(W)$, which meets the dense open $Y$. Therefore $W$ meets $p^{-1}(Y)=T_0$. Thus $T_0$ is a dense open of $T$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed pp.153-154; referenced Milne (2013), Definition 4.2 and Lemma 4.3 (read https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2). Direct local-representative proof written by Q85, replacing the graph argument.

proof.text: The morphism $G\times_kY\xrightarrow{a}Y\hookrightarrow X$ on the dense open $T_0$ defines a rational map $\alpha:T\dashrightarrow X$. By [lem-sfb-rational-map-maximal-representative], it has a unique maximal representative $\alpha:U\to X$, since $T$ is reduced by step 1 and $X$ is separated by hypothesis. Its restriction to $T_0$ is exactly the given action followed by the open inclusion, and $T_0\subseteq U$. A rational map with this restriction is the same equivalence class, so the rational extension is unique.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed pp.153-154; referenced Milne (2013), Definition 4.2 and Lemma 4.3 (read https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2). Direct local-representative proof written by Q85, replacing the graph argument.

proof.text: Let $U_e\subseteq X$ be the inverse image of $U$ under $z\mapsto(e,z)$. It is open and contains $Y$. The restriction $b:U_e\to X$, $b(z)=\alpha(e,z)$, agrees with the identity of $X$ on $Y$, by the unit law for $a$. Thus $b$ and $\mathrm{id}_X$ represent the same rational map from $X$ to $X$. The source $X$ is reduced because it is integral; the target $X$ is separated. Agreement on intersections in [lem-sfb-rational-map-maximal-representative] gives $b=\mathrm{id}_X|_{U_e}$. This proves the unit assertion for every $x$ where $e\cdot x$ is defined.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, printed pp.153-154; referenced Milne (2013), Definition 4.2 and Lemma 4.3 (read https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2). Direct local-representative proof written by Q85, replacing the graph argument.

proof.text: Fix $g,h\in G(k)$ and $x\in X(k)$ with $(h,x)\in U$ and $(g,\alpha(h,x))\in U$. Let $U_h\subseteq X$ be the open inverse image of $U$ under $z\mapsto(h,z)$, and put $b_h(z)=\alpha(h,z)$. It contains $Y$, and $b_h|_Y=a(h,-)$. On $G\times_kU_h$ the formula $L(u,z)=(uh^{-1},b_h(z))$ defines a morphism to $G\times_kX$, using multiplication by the fixed $k$-point $h^{-1}$. Put $O=L^{-1}(U)$ and $F=\alpha\circ L:O\to X$. These are an open of $T$ and a morphism on it. Since $L(gh,x)=(g,\alpha(h,x))$, the point $(gh,x)$ belongs to $O$. Moreover $T_0\subseteq O$: for $z\in Y$ the point $b_h(z)$ lies in $Y$, where all actions are defined. On $T_0$ the associativity law for the regular action gives $F(u,z)=a(uh^{-1},a(h,z))=a(u,z)$, because $(uh^{-1})h=u$. These are equalities of morphisms, by restricting the given action identity along the fixed point $h$. Thus $O$ is dense by step 1 and $F$ represents $\alpha$. By [lem-sfb-rational-map-maximal-representative], $O\subseteq U$ and $\alpha|_O=F$. Evaluating at $(gh,x)$ gives $(gh)\cdot x=F(gh,x)=g\cdot(h\cdot x)$ and proves its definedness.
